newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Firebombs blaze in Seoul as students riot.
newsitem.headline: Firebombs blaze in Seoul as students riot.

text.p: South Korea's militant students, brandishing iron pipes and crude firebombs, battled riot police in Seoul on Sunday in protests demanding the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
As many as 10,000 students took to the streets over the weekend, dashing through the city's subway system and emerging suddenly at station entrances to engage police.
Large areas of the city echoed to the sounds of splintering glass as petrol bombs fashioned from beer bottles landed at the feet of riot officers, engulfing them in sheets of flame.

Armoured police teargas launchers sent volleys of gas shells arching into the sky in response. Some officers sprayed stinging gas into the faces of demonstrators, many of them young women, from hand-held cannisters.
The worst student violence in almost a year was sparked by Kim's refusal to bow to opposition demands and reveal how much he spent on his 1992 election campaign.

Allegations that Kim grossly overspent have surfaced in the final year of his presidency in the wake of a corruption scandal involving loans to bankrupt Hanbo Steel. The scandal has led to the arrest of Kim's son and several of his closest aides, shattering his credibility.
But in a nationally televised speech last Friday, Kim conceded only that his campaign used up "enormous sums" -- and shrugged it off as a failure of the system.
He called for a radical overhaul of election spending laws, including a ban on money-guzzling mass rallies and privately-run political machines.
Other proposed changes were state funding for election campaigns and greater access by candidates to the mass media.
Hit-and-run attacks by students were carefully orchestrated by an outlawed leftwing campus body that the government alleges takes its orders from rival North Korea.
Subway trains were held up as long snakes of students scampered on foot along the tracks through long tunnels deep beneath the city.

Among the students were members of far left groups affilitated to international socialist organisations. But most were fresh-faced undergraduates clad in jeans and sporting baseball caps, and carrying firebombs in backpacks.
"Bring down Kim Young-sam", "Reveal the Election Funds", they chanted for the third day of protests.
Some of the worst fighting on Saturday night occurred outside the five-star Shilla Hotel, a favourite for visiting heads of state.

Tourist buses dodged rock-throwing students to get in and out, and had to ferry terrified passengers at high speed through an intersection slickened by blazing firebombs. Surrounding streets were littered with spent teargas shells.
Casualty details were not known, but in one dramatic incident on Saturday a student fell screaming to the ground with his shirt on fire.
Media reports said another student was in critical condition after suffering a heart attack during Friday's protests.

South Korea's student movement, which seemed to have been crushed when 151 leaders were jailed following a campus uprising last year, has burst back to life on a popular wave of anger against the president.
Political analysts said President Kim would have to move swiftly on legal reform before public outrage, student unrest and pressure from opposition parties overwhelmed his administration.
Some expected a reform package would be hurried through an extraordinary session of parliament this month.
